verdict_reason: The type step and the new landing check are correct, but the module loads the backend client and config for one enum, and the seed's use is a bare literal outside the ROLES owner.

todos.issue: seed-address.js:1 imports ADDRESS_TYPES from services/address-book/index.js, which also loads client.js (config.js with strict convict validation at load, @defra/hapi-tracing) and stub.js. That file only re-exports the constant from address-types.js. tests/lighthouse/auth-setup.cjs requires this module inside the lhci process, so every Lighthouse URL run now loads the app's backend client and config just to read one enum.
todos.fix: Must: the Lighthouse scripts read the address type and role constants from the module that owns them (address-types.js) and load none of the address-book backend client or app config. One way: import { ADDRESS_TYPES, ROLES } from '../../src/server/app/services/address-book/address-types.js'.

todos.issue: seed-address.js:73 posts roles: 'PLACE_OF_ORIGIN' as a bare literal, while the type on line 55 comes from ADDRESS_TYPES. ROLES and ROLES_BY_ADDRESS_TYPE in address-types.js own both the role values and which roles each type offers. If PLACE_OF_ORIGIN is renamed or stops being offered for ORIGIN_OR_CONSIGNOR, no unit test fails. The seed only breaks at run time against a live stack.
todos.fix: Must: the seed's use comes from the address-types owner and is one that the chosen type offers, so a change there breaks the seed's unit tests. One way: roles: ROLES.PLACE_OF_ORIGIN, plus a #SEED_ADDRESS test that asserts ROLES_BY_ADDRESS_TYPE[ADDRESS_TYPES.ORIGIN_OR_CONSIGNOR] contains it, or hold type and roles together in one exported seed constant.

todos.issue: seed-address.js:58-61 and :79-83 report only posted.status. A 302 to the wrong place reads 'did not move on to the add form (302)' with no location. createSeedAddress now also refuses a 302 that lands on another tab, and still says the page 'rejected the seed address (302) — its fields have moved on'. That save may have succeeded, so the message sends the reader to the wrong cause.
todos.fix: Must: each refusal names the status and the location it got, and the createSeedAddress message tells a refused save apart from a save that landed somewhere unexpected. One way: include posted.location in both messages and branch the createSeedAddress message on status === HTTP_FOUND.
